To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we demonstrate classification of clinical skin images using a deep convolutional neural network trained from scratch, achieving performance on par with board certified dermatologists for two critical binary classification tasks: keratinocyte carcinoma versus benign seborreic keratosis; and malignant melanoma versus benign nevus.

a deep CNN trained from scratch on a large dataset of clinical images, achieves performance on par or better than 21 board certified expert dermatologists for the binary classification of skin cancer, with a sensitivity and specificity of 0.94 and 0.95, respectively, for the identification of keratinocyte carcinoma and a sensitivity and specificity 0.86 and 0.96, respectively, for melanoma.

a CNN trained on images of skin lesions alone, without any additional information such as clinical history, can match dermatologists in the diagnosis of skin cancer, and that this CNN can be implemented on a mobile device.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a deep learning algorithm for automated skin lesion analysis.
the application of deep learning to the problem of automated skin lesion diagnosis.
the development of an AI capable of classifying a broad set of dermatological conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a deep convolutional neural network trained end to end using only pixels and labels can achieve a level of competence for skin cancer classification comparable to dermatologists, and that this network can be deployed on a smartphone to extend the reach of a dermatologist to any person in the world with a smartphone.
the CNN is a powerful diagnostic tool, capable of achieving dermatologist-level classification of skin cancer.
a deep neural network can classify skin cancer at the level of a dermatologist.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a deep convolutional neural network that is capable of classifying the most common cancers and most deadly skin cancer with a dermatologist level of competence.
deep learning is a powerful approach that is able to learn from large amounts of data to achieve performance on par with dermatologists.
deep neural networks can classify skin cancer at the level of dermatologists, and therefore can provide an artificial intelligence capable to assist dermatologists in clinical practice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single CNN can be trained end to end to achieve dermatologist level performance in skin lesion classification, a task which requires a high level of visual understanding and clinical expertise.
a CNN can be used to classify skin cancer from a dermoscopic image.
a deep CNN can be trained to perform at the level of a board certified dermatologist for two of the most critical tasks in skin cancer diagnosis.
